name: Chunk Claims
pages: Players can {b}claim chunks{/} to protect their land, belongings, or builds. To claim a chunk, first open the {l:user_interface/map/}world map{/l} with {k:journeymap.map_toggle_alt/k}.{pb}Hold {k:journeypac.claim_mode/k} while using {c}Left Button{/c} to select the area you want to claim (or using {c}Right Button{/c} to {b}unclaim{/}). You can only create claims up to {!}8 chunks{/} away from your current location.

The name of the player or party who has claimed a chunk will appear above your hotbar when you enter it. Unclaimed chunks will show "{b}Wilderness{/}" instead.{pb}The key to open the {b}parties and claims menu{/} is {k:gui.xaero_pac_key_open_menu/k}. The menu includes a button to {b}Claim{/} the chunk you are currently in, an {b}About{/} button to show details of your {b}party{/} (if you are in one), and the {b}Player Config Menu{/}.

From the Player Config Menu, you can fine-tune the details of your claims in {b}My Player Config{/}.{pb}A {b}sub-config{/} is a profile for a set of claimed chunks, each with its own {!}name{/}, {!}color{/}, and {!}protections{/}. By default, all players have a single sub-config called "main", but more can be added from this menu.

The {b}Sub-Config to Edit{/} can be changed to switch to a different sub-config. You can switch to using that sub-config when claiming chunks by clicking {b}Claim With [name]{/}, or delete the sub-config by clicking {b}Delete [name]{/}. To create a {b}New Sub-Config{/}, enter the name of the profile in the text box and click the checkmark to confirm.

The {b}Party Name{/} will be the name of the party you own. This will be blank by default, but can be edited if desired. (See {l:user_interface/parties/}this chapter{/l} for more on that!){pb}The remaining options on the config menu are to control what {b}protections{/} {!}do{/} or {!}don't{/} apply to your claims. Be careful with these settings, since they can affect mob behavior or prevent your contraptions from working as expected.
